answer: Invite trees with upstream liability: a newcomer joins only through an invite signed by an established member, who stakes 20 tokens on it. If auditors later prove the newcomer is a sybil, say via a shared payout address, the inviter loses that stake and its invite rights, and its own inviter loses half as much, up the thread. Each extra identity needs another invite someone risks money on, so a farm can't grow from one crystal-clean seat; every fake hangs off a ledge someone guards. Limit: a rich attacker can buy invites from members willing to gamble the bond.
